steps.name: Sample structure QC on delivered counts
caveats: A sample whose library size is several times below the study median must not be deleted in silence: keep it through the QC, inspect it on the PCA and the distance heatmap, report its library size and detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. DESeq2 down-weights a low-depth sample through its size factor, so removal is a judgment and not a default.

The delivered DESeq2 results were fitted on all 12 samples, so any QC conclusion here can only qualify the interpretation — it cannot alter the ranked list used downstream.

plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question asks only which hallmark pathways change between treated (psoriasis lesional) and control skin; the differential expression is already done and delivered as /data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns, DESeq2 treated vs control contrast). The plan therefore does no new differential test and adds no unasked scope.

Step T1S1 is a short sample-structure check on the delivered counts (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 12 samples plus the gene-symbol column; metadata.csv, 12 rows x 2 columns, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch). It exists because the data profile flags sample_01 at roughly 4x below the median library size, and because an enrichment on a delivered results table should be preceded by a sample-level check of the counts when the counts are delivered too. It is diagnostic only: blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes and detected genes per sample. sample_01 is kept and reported, not removed — depth alone is not a reason to drop a sample, and the delivered DESeq2 table was fitted with all 12 samples anyway, so dropping it here could not change the enrichment input. If sample_01 or any other sample sits away from its condition group, that is reported as a caveat on the interpretation of the delivered contrast, not acted on.

Step T2S1 is the analysis the question asks for: fgsea preranked GSEA of all tested genes in de_results.csv against the 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat`-type column of the delivered table). The Wald statistic is the stated choice among the three defensible ranking metrics, because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, so a large but noisy low-count fold change does not float to the top. The full ranked list is used — no threshold on padj or log2FC before the test — since the point of the ranked method is to detect coordinated small changes. Gene sets are intersected with the tested genes and kept at 15-500 members; the universe is the tested genes only. Identifiers in both the results table and the hallmark GMT are HGNC symbols, so the ranking runs in symbol space with no cross-space mapping, and the unmapped/dropped share is reported. The direction convention is inherited from the delivered table: positive log2_fold_change means higher in treated (lesional) than control; the step must verify and restate this from the column names before assigning a direction to any pathway.

Step T1S3 assembles the report: the significant hallmark sets at BH-adjusted p < 0.05 with NES and direction, the leading-edge genes of each with their gene-level statistics, the overlap between leading edges (hallmark sets share genes; overlapping sets are one finding, not several), and the full reproducibility record — collection name and release (MSigDB 2026.1 human hallmark), rank metric, universe, size window, tool versions, permutation seed, and sessionInfo. It also carries the two honest caveats: enrichment results are method-dependent and a hallmark hit is a hypothesis, and the QC observations on sample_01 bound how firmly the underlying contrast can be read.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark
Enrichment report with leading edge, collection version, rank metric, universe, size window, reproducibility record
